profile_text.body:
Runway is a for-profit startup founded in 2018 and headquartered in New York, NY, with a European headquarters recently opened in London. The company describes itself as building foundational "Real-World Intelligence" that can understand, simulate, and act in the world, and it offers products and services built on top of that intelligence. Its core technical offering is GWM-1, which it describes as a state-of-the-art General World Model, used to power components ranging from policy inference and evaluation to synthetic data generation. The company also offers the Runway Media Router, described as the first preference-optimized router for generative media, built into the Runway Dev platform. Runway has announced a planned $100M investment in the UK AI ecosystem alongside its London expansion.

Runway's primary tracked product is its video generation platform at runwayml.com, categorized under video generation and editing. The company has published findings from what it describes as hundreds of enterprises using Runway for media production, citing cost and speed gains in creative workflows.

On the legal front, Runway faces notable litigation exposure. It is a named defendant in multiple cases in the Southern District of New York, including suits brought by David Vance Gardner, Businessing LLC, and Ace Cam, Inc., as well as a separate Gardner case in the Central District of California. Runway is also a party in the Andersen v. Stability AI case in the Northern District of California, which involves multiple AI companies. The held facts record 260 legal data points associated with New York jurisdiction.
